spec.title: Connect time p99 per cell (client side)
spec.description: k6_http_req_connecting_seconds for the burst requests only. Look for: ~0 s when the queue was big enough, about 3 s when the first SYN and the 1 s retry were both dropped (prediction in the README). Surprising: values near 1 s only (the stall ended earlier than I think) or values above 7 s (a third retry). Caveat: k6 series are not marked stale, so the last value of a finished cell can linger for minutes; read the legend 'max' per cell.

spec.title: Waiting time p99 per cell (request sent -> first byte)
spec.description: k6_http_req_waiting_seconds for the burst. Connections that were already in the accept queue should wait about 1.3 s (they sit there until the stall ends). Surprising: waiting close to 0 for all cells means the stall did not block the loop when the burst arrived.

spec.title: Total request time p99 per cell
spec.description: k6_http_req_duration_seconds p99 for the burst. Prediction: about 1.3-1.5 s when nothing overflowed, about 3.0-3.2 s when some connections overflowed (they paid the SYN retries). With the 2 s client timeout (B4) the overflowed ones are cut off.

spec.title: Outcomes: ok / timeout / reset / other (per cell, cumulative)
spec.description: Counters from my k6 script (MISSING until the script has run once: see missing-metrics.txt). Each series is the final count of that outcome for the cell. Prediction: with default settings all connections end 'ok' (just late); timeouts only in B4, resets only in B2. Surprising: any 'other' (the script prints the raw error text, check the k6 output).

spec.title: Connections that needed a SYN retry (connect >= 900 ms)
spec.description: k6_e08_connect_slow_total (MISSING until the script has run once). Roughly the number of connections whose first SYN was dropped. Compare with the ListenOverflows panel in row 2: overflow events should be about 2x this number because each such client was dropped twice (first try and the 1 s retry).

spec.title: Accept queue length vs backlog the kernel is really using
spec.description: ep_listen_recvq = connections waiting in the accept queue; ep_listen_sendq = the backlog in use = min(listen backlog, somaxconn). Prediction: recvq peaks at backlog+1 (when the burst is bigger) and sendq equals the number in the cell name (B1: 16 even though Node asked for 511). Caveat: the exporter writes every 0.25 s and Prometheus scrapes every 1 s, so short peaks can be missed; the 10 Hz CSV in captures/<testid>.queue.csv is the high-resolution record.

spec.title: ListenOverflows and ListenDrops per second
spec.description: node_netstat_TcpExt_ListenOverflows / ListenDrops from node_exporter. Each increment is one connection attempt (SYN or final ACK) refused because the accept queue was full. System-wide counters: any other listener on the machine counts too. Prediction: about 2 x (burst - backlog - 1) per overflow cell (two retry waves are dropped while the loop is still blocked). Surprising: ListenDrops much larger than ListenOverflows, or any increments in cells where burst < backlog.

spec.title: ListenOverflows total over the dashboard range
spec.description: increase() of node_netstat_TcpExt_ListenOverflows over the whole selected time range. Set the range to cover one cell to get the per-cell number; compare with deltas.tsv written by step.sh.

spec.title: ListenDrops total over the dashboard range
spec.description: Same as the left panel for node_netstat_TcpExt_ListenDrops.

spec.title: SYN retransmits, TCP timeouts and RSTs sent
spec.description: TcpExt TCPSynRetrans and TCPTimeouts show the client side retry timers firing (loopback: client and server are the same machine, so both ends count). Tcp_OutRsts jumps in B2 (tcp_abort_on_overflow=1). Surprising: lots of RSTs in cells with abort_on_overflow=0.

spec.title: Connections accepted by Node vs connections completed by k6
spec.description: http_connections_total (Node's own accepted-connection counter) against k6_http_reqs_total for the burst. Both should end up equal when everything succeeds; the shape differs: Node accepts everything in a spike right after the stall ends, k6 sees the late ones 1.7 s later. Caveat: Node's /metrics is unreachable during the stall (scrape timeout 1 s), so the server series has a gap there.

spec.title: Server-side p99 vs client-side p99
spec.description: The point of the experiment in one panel: the server's own request duration (starts when Node parses the request) cannot see the time spent in the accept queue or in SYN retries, so it stays tiny while k6 sees seconds. I filter route!~"/metrics|/stall" but I have not verified that the label is called 'route'; if it is not, the 1.5 s /stall request will show up here and spoil the comparison.

spec.title: Proof the event loop was blocked (scrape failures + loop lag)
spec.description: up{job=eventpulse-nodejs} drops to 0 when Prometheus cannot scrape /metrics during the stall (scrape_timeout is 1 s, the stall is 1.5 s). nodejs_eventloop_lag_max_seconds is the loop delay seen right after the stall ends. Prediction: about 1.3-1.5 s lag in stall cells, about 0 in the B3 controls.

spec.title: Node process CPU (user vs system)
spec.description: process_cpu_*_seconds_total of the server. During the stall user CPU is ~1 core (the busy loop); right after it, system CPU rises while Node accepts hundreds of connections in one go. Surprising: high CPU in the no-stall controls.

spec.title: Host CPU by mode (all CPUs, in cores)
spec.description: node_cpu_seconds_total without idle. Shows if the machine as a whole is busy (generator + server + kernel).

spec.title: Context switches per second
spec.description: node_context_switches_total. A burst of hundreds of connections should show a short spike.

spec.title: Open fds and open connections (server)
spec.description: process_open_fds vs http_connections_open. Burst of 1000 should stay far below the fd limit (about 1000 vs the limit in process_max_fds).

spec.title: Generator vs server vs sampler CPU (per pinned group)
spec.description: Busy % of the CPUs I pinned: k6 on 1,2,3,7,8,9 (keep under about 70%), server on 0,6, sampler on 4. If the cpu label is not the plain number on this machine the panel is empty. A saturated k6 group means the connect timings are the generator's fault, not the kernel's.

spec.title: k6 iterations per cell (must equal burst + 1, or burst without stall)
spec.description: max of k6_iterations_total per cell. Expected: 51, 201, 1001 in stall cells and 200 in the B3 controls. A smaller number means some VUs never ran (k6 could not start them: generator problem). k6_dropped_iterations_total is also drawn; it does not apply to per-VU iterations, so it should be 'no data' or 0.

spec.title: k6 failed-request rate per cell
spec.description: k6_http_req_failed_rate. 0 in all cells except B4 (timeouts) and B2 (resets, if any). A non-zero rate anywhere else needs an explanation.

spec.title: TIME_WAIT sockets (host)
spec.description: node_sockstat_TCP_tw. 1000-connection cells leave about 1000 TIME_WAIT sockets for 60 s. The settle step only waits above 3000. Not a correctness issue for the accept queue.

spec.title: Scrape health: node_exporter and server
spec.description: up for job=node and job=eventpulse-nodejs. The server target flaps to 0 during every stall (expected). node_exporter must stay at 1.

spec.title: Listen overflows in the idle baseline (should be flat)
spec.description: Cumulative node_netstat_TcpExt_ListenOverflows. It must be flat before the first cell and between cells; a rising line there means something else on this machine is overflowing a listen queue.

spec.title: 1. The verdict: what did the burst connections experience?
2. The mechanism: the accept queue and the kernel counters
3. Resource view: where the cost lands
4. Validity checks: can I trust this run?
